title: Pizza Bot 把 AI agent 装进收件箱，异步工作终于可管理
summary: Pizza Bot 用 Unread 和 Action 两个队列区分完成与待审批，把后台 AI agent 的工作流变成可批量处理的收件箱。
opening: Pizza Bot 是一个自托管的桌面应用，它把后台运行的 AI agent 任务映射到一个类似电子邮件的收件箱界面。完成的工作进入 Unread，等待审批的操作进入 Action。这个设计解决了一个关键问题：当 AI agent 从同步对话转向异步执行时，用户如何管理多个并发任务而不被实时打断。但桌面应用的形态也带来了新的限制——计算机关闭时任务无法运行，除非部署独立后端。
core_experience:
Pizza Bot 的核心体验围绕收件箱展开。用户启动或调度任务后，agent 在后台持续工作，完成的结果出现在 Unread 队列，需要用户批准的操作出现在 Action 队列。这种设计将 agent 的异步执行与用户的注意力管理解耦：用户不必盯着聊天窗口等待输出，而是像处理邮件一样在方便时批量查看和决策。

产品通过有状态的 DeepAgents/LangGraph 运行时支持 checkpoint，使任务在客户端断开后仍能继续，并通过 cron 或 webhook 触发新任务。同时，它把 agent 的能力扩展为工具范围的子代理（skills），其进度显示在 Activity 面板中，进一步将复杂任务分解为可观察的单元。

在文件访问方面，Pizza Bot 默认不授予主目录访问权限，用户需在 Settings > Files 中显式添加只读或可写文件夹。这种设计增强了用户对数据可控性的信任。
why_it_works:
Pizza Bot 有效的原因在于它解决了 AI agent 从同步对话向异步工作流转变时的核心交互问题。传统聊天界面要求用户保持会话活跃，而长时间任务会占用注意力并造成上下文断裂。Pizza Bot 用收件箱隐喻重新组织工作状态：Unread 和 Action 队列提供了清晰的优先级和决策点，降低了用户管理多个并发 agent 任务的认知负担。

人工审批机制（human-in-the-loop）将高风险操作的控制权保留给用户，同时允许低风险任务自动完成，平衡了效率与安全。支持多种模型提供商和本地模型（Ollama）降低了使用门槛，而显式的文件访问授权增强了信任。这些设计共同创造了一个可预测、可审计的 agent 工作环境。
boundaries:
Pizza Bot 的桌面应用形态限制了真正的异步性：计算机关闭时任务无法运行，除非部署独立后端。与现有工单系统（如 Linear）或简单文件监控方案相比，Pizza Bot 的差异化价值尚不明确。如果用户已经在使用 Linear 或 Jira 等工单系统，Pizza Bot 必须证明其本地优先、模型无关和审批流设计能带来显著优势。

此外，产品缺乏对结构化输出的强制机制，用户可能需要额外集成 MCP 服务器或插件。长期记忆的具体实现和存储方式未公开，可能影响用户对数据可控性的信任。
personal_judgment:
Pizza Bot 代表了一类重要的产品方向：将 AI agent 从对话工具转变为可管理的后台工作系统。收件箱范式是明智的选择，因为它利用了用户已有的心智模型，降低了学习成本。然而，产品目前仍处于早期阶段，其核心价值主张需要更清晰地与现有解决方案区分。

我认为 Pizza Bot 最有价值的贡献是提出了 agent 工作管理的交互模式，但产品要获得广泛采用，还需要解决部署灵活性、结构化输出和与现有工具链的集成问题。

transferable_methods.name: 收件箱式任务队列
transferable_methods.principle: 将异步 agent 的输出和待审批操作分别放入独立的队列（如 Unread 和 Action），使用户可以按自己的节奏处理，而不是被实时对话打断。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于需要长时间运行、多任务并行且结果需要人工审核的 AI agent 工作流。

transferable_methods.name: 人工审批与自动执行分离
transferable_methods.principle: 通过 human-in-the-loop 机制，将高风险操作标记为需要用户批准，而低风险任务自动完成，从而在效率和安全性之间取得平衡。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于涉及敏感数据修改、外部通信或资源消耗的 agent 任务。

product_takeaway: AI 产品经理可以从 Pizza Bot 学到：将 agent 工作流映射到用户熟悉的交互范式（如收件箱）可以显著降低管理成本。但产品必须解决部署灵活性和与现有工具链的集成，才能真正融入用户的工作流。

sources.title: pizza-bot
sources.excerpt:
Pizza Bot

An inbox for long-running AI work.
Start or schedule a task, walk away, and come back to finished work in Unread and decisions waiting for you in Action.

Download · Quick start · Why Pizza Bot · Extend · Architecture · Contributing · Roadmap · Discussions

![Pizza Bot inbox showing unread work, an approval request, a completed launch brief, and delegated agent activity](docs/assets/pizza-bot-inbox.png) Agents keep working when you navigate away or disconnect; only the api-server process must remain running. A stateful DeepAgents/LangGraph runtime serves the same React experience in Electron and the browser, and the desktop app, web app, and terminal CLI all talk to the api-server over HTTP/SSE. Pizza Bot was developed at Amazon and is released under the Apache 2.0 license. ## Why Pizza Bot? - **Work asynchronously.** Switch conversations without stopping their runs. - **Return to the right queue.** Completed work lands in Unread; durable approval requests land in Action. - **Organize conversations.** Group threads into folders without hiding matching work from the global Unread and Action queues. - **Resume real work.** Checkpointed runs survive client disconnects, and cron or webhook triggers can start work without an open conversation. - **Delegate to specialists.** Skills become tool-scoped subagents whose progress appears in the Activity panel. - **Bring your model provider.** Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Ollama are supported. - **Keep control of consequential actions.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, long-term memory, file attachments, and desktop notifications are built into the workflow. - **Grant local access explicitly.** Add individual read-only or writable folders under **Settings > Files**; Pizza Bot receives no default home-directory access. ## Download Installers are attached to every [release](https://github.com/pizza-bot-app/pizza-bot/releases/latest), with a `SHA256SUMS` to check a download against. | Platform | Packages | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple silicon, Intel) | `.dmg`, `.zip` | Signed and notarized | | Windows (x64) | `-setup.exe` | | | Linux (x64, arm64) | `.deb`, `.rpm` | Not signed; verify against `SHA256SUMS` | ## Quick start Node.js 24 or newer is required. ```bash npm install npm run build npm run dev ``` `npm run dev` starts the Vite frontend and Electron desktop shell. The shell forks and supervises its own api-server, matching the packaged application's process model. Configure a model under **Settings > Providers** before starting a live run. See [Running from source](docs/RUNNING.md) for isolated data roots, browser and CLI development, desktop packages, and remote backends. ## Ways to run | Experience | Best for | Start here | | --- | --- | --- | | Electron desktop | Local inbox with an embedded backend | `npm run dev` | | Browser | Web development or static deployment | [Browser development](docs/RUNNING.md#browser-development) | | Terminal CLI | Scripts, terminals, and remote backends | [CLI](docs/RUNNING.md#cli) | | Standalone backend | Remote Electron, browsers, containers, or Linux services | [Backend guide](docs/STANDALONE_BACKEND.md) | A running api-server needs access to at least one model provider; HTTP clients do not. Configure Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or Ollama in **Settings > Providers**. Bedrock accepts an AWS profile, AWS access keys, or a Bedrock API key, with an optional region

sources.excerpt:
congrats on the public launch! it's been clear to me for a while now that agents will need their own ways to communicate and an asynchronous inbox/task system is a necessity already. will point my agents at the repo to see how we can leverage
I have a more basic question; I am trying to understand its purpose. How does this compare with connecting your agent to your ticket tracker? Linear can dispatch the agents: https://linear.app/agents https://linear.app/docs/coding-sessions If it is about local work, how does it compare with simply having your agent monitor a directory for ticket files?
Why does it have to be a desktop app vs a self hostable web app? That way it can truly run asynchronously, even with the computer switched off.
This looks great. I've been playing around with GrokBot, and like a lot of what it does, but would much, much prefer an open source project to manage various asynchronous tasks. What I like about GrokBot is the combination of freeform agent discussions, scheduled jobs, agent-to-agent communication, per-agent memory, and the fact that they all get a sandboxed instance with a browser. It's very well implemented. I think they have a very similar vision to yours.
Do you have a list of a few mcp servers or other tools you would add to help with the pizza-bot specific workflow? For example, how would you enforce structured output, should that be an mcp server, a plugin, already in the box?
